### 1. What's Life Like in This Ward?
On hot summer afternoons reaching over 34°C, walking outside feels unbearable because there are zero parks and officially not a single recorded shade tree on our streets. When sudden rains hit, roads turn into rivers within minutes because 98% of our streets have no drains to carry the water away. For families living in our dense bastis, hot tin roofs turn rooms into ovens, and dirty water backs up easily since 80% of slum homes lack underground sewer pipes.

---

### 2. Problems and What We Can Do About Them

| Problem | How Bad Is It? | Why Does This Happen Here? | What Can Be Done? |
|:---|:---|:---|:---|
| **Street flooding (Pani bharaav)** | Over 98% of roads have no working rainwater drains. | Rainwater has nowhere to run, so it pools on roads and enters shops. | Clean choked naalas, put trash screens, and build small roadside pits to catch water. |
| **Scorching heat** | Summer temperatures touch over 34°C, heating up metal roofs. | Tin sheets trap burning heat inside homes with no breeze. | Coat roofs with white heat-reflecting paint to keep indoor rooms cooler. |
| **No green shade** | Officially 0 recorded shade trees and 0 public parks. | Concrete roads and buildings leave no open space for trees to grow. | Plant leafy local trees along 3 km of walking roads and bus stops. |
| **Dirty sewage water** | 80% of slum homes are not connected to underground sewer lines. | Toilet and kitchen waste often spill into open roadside gutters. | Clear main drains of sludge and trash so dirty water does not spill into lanes. |
| **Water shortage** | 32,318 residents depend heavily on erratic tanker supplies. | Good monsoon rainwater washes away into dirty gutters instead of being saved. | Install rooftop rainwater collection tanks on 15 municipal buildings to store water. |

---

### 3. How Will the Money, Workers and Time Be Used?

| Work To Be Done | How Many? | Money (Rs.) | Workers Needed | Time Needed | Who Is Responsible? |
|:---|:---|:---|:---|:---|:---|
| Rooftop rainwater collection tanks | 15 buildings | Rs. 3,300,000 | 45 person-months | 2 months | PMC Water Supply Department |
| Shaded bus stops with drinking water kiosks | 12 stops | Rs. 2,160,000 | 30 person-months | 2 months | PMPML & PMC Health Department |
| White heat-reflecting paint for rooftops | 15 building clusters | Rs. 1,800,000 | 30 person-months | 1 month | PMC Building & Development Department |
| Tree planting for roadside shade | 3 km corridor | Rs. 750,000 | 12 person-months | 3 months | PMC Garden Department / Tree Authority |
| Cleaning major naalas and putting trash screens | 2 drain sections | Rs. 700,000 | 10 person-months | 1 month | PMC Drainage & Sewerage Department |
| Roadside rain garden to soak up runoff | 1 site | Rs. 280,000 | 3 person-months | 2 months | PMC Road Department / SWD |

- **Total money being used:** Rs. 8,990,000 out of Rs. 9,000,000  
- **Money left over:** Rs. 10,000  
- **Workers needed:** 130.0 person-months  
- **Everything done in:** 3 months  

---

### 4. What Should the Ward Officer Do? (Step by Step)

1. **Weeks 1–2:** Clear plastic, muck, and silt from the 2 major naalas and fit iron trash screens so water can move freely. At the same time, pick the 15 building clusters that need white roof paint urgently.
2. **Month 1:** Paint the roofs of the selected 15 building clusters with white heat-reflecting paint before the summer peak. Start setting up the 12 shaded bus stops and clean drinking water points.
3. **Month 2:** Build the rooftop rainwater collection tanks on 15 municipal buildings. Dig out the roadside rain garden so street rainwater can soak straight into the ground.
4. **Month 3:** Plant hardy, local shade trees along the 3 km walking stretch, put tree guards around them, and make sure local sweepers water them daily.

---

### 5. How Will Residents Know Things Are Getting Better?

- ✅ After heavy showers, water on main roads drains away within 30–45 minutes instead of staying knee-deep for hours.
- ✅ Rooms under white-painted roofs feel noticeably cooler in the afternoon, allowing families to rest comfortably without burning hot tin sheets overhead.
- ✅ Commuters and auto drivers waiting along Nagar Road have cool drinking water and deep shade at 12 bus stops instead of standing in the blistering sun.
